claims.explanation: Norethindrone acetate is a progesterone receptor (PR) agonist, and its selective killing likely depends on PR expression, which is absent in most of the least affected lines (e.g., T47D is PR-negative in the used subline, and many lung and kidney lines lack PR). The most sensitive lines include several with high PR expression (e.g., endometrial, thyroid, and some mesenchymal tumors), and the virtual cell response shows downregulation of proliferation genes (MYC, PCNA, CDK1) consistent with PR-mediated growth arrest. TP53 mutation is common in sensitive lines but also in resistant lines, so it is not a strong predictor; instead, PR expression and possibly AR expression (due to cross-reactivity) may drive sensitivity.

features.basis: PR is the primary target; sensitive lines likely express PR, while many resistant lines (e.g., T47D subline, lung, kidney) lack it.
Norethindrone can cross-react with androgen receptor; virtual cell top match is ostarine (AR modulator), and sensitive lines include AR-positive prostate? (VCAP is AR+).
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but many resistant lines have wild-type or unknown TP53; however, sensitive lines also have TP53 mutations, so this is weak.
CDKN2A loss may increase dependence on hormone signaling; observed in several sensitive lines (KELLY, IPC298, K029AX).
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which can cross-talk with PR; seen in sensitive FTC133 and 786O (resistant) so not consistent.
NF1 mutations in sensitive lines (BICR6, FTC133) may lead to RAS/MAPK activation, potentially sensitizing to hormonal therapy.
ATM mutations in sensitive lines (SNU685, RKN, SNUC5) may impair DNA repair, increasing sensitivity to hormonal stress.
KMT2D mutations in sensitive lines (BICR6, SNUC5, KU1919) suggest epigenetic dysregulation may enhance response.
BRAF mutations appear in both sensitive (IGR37, SNUC5, K029AX) and resistant (CAL12T) lines, so not predictive.
EGFR mutations are common in resistant lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006) and some sensitive lines (KNS81, KYSE70), so inconsistent.
KRAS mutations in sensitive lines (RKN, CL11, T3M4) but also in resistant PATU8988S, so weak.
SMARCA4 mutations in resistant lines (SKNSH, COV434) suggest chromatin remodeling defects may reduce sensitivity.
